what: the corpus lane's lists of the spaces our own build made in a provider's text, kept here byte for byte in the folders the lane keeps them in: for each served text that holds one, the places that close at print. One entry per relay whose lists are read, and each list is read with the receipt its entry names. A relay that reissues an earlier relay's lists takes its place and names it (replaces); a receipt that read a store the page never served as such says what that store is (read_at); the files a relay sent beside its lists are kept and named (beside, meets)

lists_rule.what: the rule the lists themselves were built under: relay v168's, unchanged, which this relay's receipt names by this sha256

read_at.what: the receipt read the page's store 4d1357b26ca5 with all 4,252 lines of relay v188's landing list laid on it, a store no page ever served as such (the relay's RULE.md, «The store after v188»); the counts it states are held on the served store by the second road (tools/made-spaces-second-road-v1.mjs)

beside.what: the lane's own verifier's receipt of these lists
the 106 lines that differ from relay v168's lists: 14 new, 92 whose counts change

meets.what: the lane's own count of where these lists meet relays v187, v189 and v190 and the lines of v188 the page does not land; tools/check-made-spaces-v1.mjs holds the page's second road to it

replaces.kept: in made-spaces-v1/, as the record of the first reading (store 90d9eb8e7082); no tool reads its lists or its receipt, and its RULE.md is the rule of the lists that replace them (lists_rule)

receipt.what: the lane's builder run again on the store its landing v188 makes: relay v188.1 sent it with the same two lists, byte for byte (its v2.1 files are these v2 files), and it takes the place of relay v178's own receipt

read_at.what: the receipt read the page's store 4d1357b26ca5 with all 4,252 lines of relay v188's landing list laid on it, a store no page ever served as such (the relay's RULE.md, «The store after v188»); the counts it states are held on the served store by the second road (tools/made-spaces-second-road-v1.mjs)

never_closed.what: the served texts of the same source that lost a word of the provider's, with the places where a space stands for it: the provider's own space, which no list closes

beside.what: the lane's own verifier's receipt of that run

words_back.what: the corpus lane's list of the unabridged BDB's openings of a numbered sense that lost words to our build, each with BDB's words given back (words_back), the places of it that close at print (closes), the note as it prints (prints), the closes slot 9 holds today (route_closes) and its status; keyed by key and rank as relay v174 keys the rows, and to land by key and rank, never by text. Beside it, the openings relay v178 counted among them whose own opening lost nothing (in-921-lost-none), and the lane's four receipts of the two roads that made and proved the list. The owner's questions 17 and 18 of 14 November 2026 are taken (OWNER-QUESTIONS-2026-11-14.md: «just push the ledgers we did live»): the settled rows land with the done rows, the held rows stay notes with gaps

receipts.what: road 1: the catalog's own step replayed, every one of relay v174's rows held to it
the order of BDB's Hebrew where pieces stand side by side, settled by the witness
road 2: the provider's file read with no catalog code; it agrees on every line
relay v174's rows read on the page's served store 4d1357b26ca5: all 2,008 stand at their key and rank with their text

words_back.not_kept: the lane's scripts (build-words-back-v1.mjs, settle-hebrew-order-v1.mjs, verify-words-back-v1.mjs, check-page-store-v1.mjs, and the ship-v187 folder's) and its step before the final list (words-back-v1.jsonl): nothing of another lane's is run in this tree, and the letter names each by its sha256

retext.what: the rows that land, one line per row in the list's order: { action retext, m, key, rank, route (as served), to_text (its words_back), from_slot words_back, closes, route_closes ([] for none), prints, opens (the sense the row opens), status, from (relay, list, line) }: 740 rows, 512 done and 228 settled by the witness, 88 of them carrying 140 closes; tools/strike-rows-v1.mjs lands them (row-strike-rule-v7)

held.what: the lines held, one per line in the list's order: { m, key, rank, route, status, held_because (seam, or the lane's own status), seam (how it is made, its kinds, its places in prints) where it is one, from }: 49 lines, 11 where the printed text sets a Hebrew character against a Latin letter or a digit (8 made inside words_back, 3 by a close), 36 held by the lane for an unsettled Hebrew order and 2 for a damaged provider file; they stay notes with gaps, and the 11 go back to the lane

landed_by.reason: the owner's call 11 of 13 November 2026 (give BDB's words back) and questions 17 and 18 of 14 November, taken as recommended: relay v187's words back land by key and rank, 740 rows (512 done, 228 settled by the witness), each proved on the store by tools/derive-words-back-v1.mjs (words-back-landing-rule-v1); 49 lines are held (11 where the printed text sets a Hebrew character against a Latin letter or a digit, 36 unsettled, 2 damaged)

derived.what: the lists tools/derive-words-back-v1.mjs derives from the lane's list, every line proved again on the store, and writes beside this pin only as these bytes; not kept in the tree: the store steps write them before the round that lands the first

note_print.says: a line's note is the provider's remark on its own file standing inside the text (relay v168's RULE.md, «A note»). Where the text prints, the remark is taken out with the closes, its words and the spaces our build made on either side of them, so the text prints as the line's prints_without_the_note; its words ride on the row in slot 9's third place, { words, by }, and the card prints them apart as the file's own note, credited to the provider whose file it is (tools/apply-made-spaces-v1.mjs)
note_print.by_is: the provider whose file each listed source's notes stand on: Open Scriptures, whose HebrewLexicon file HebrewStrong.xml relay v188.1's receipt reads (inputs.provider)
note_print.ruling: the owner, 16 November 2026, card 3 of the four cards (wip/2026-11-16/the-four-cards/FOUR-CARDS-2026-11-16.md, «ok go ahead»), taken under the owner's rule of 15 November («just push the ledgers we did live»): Strong's words print without the remark, «a sister (used very widely [like 251], literally and figuratively)» (the list's prints_without_the_note), and under it the remark as the file's note, «number 250, corrected to 251» (the list's note.words). The corpus lane's receipt leaned so (note_branch: «as a note»)

note: every sha256 here is the one the relay's letter names for the file, and the bytes taken hash to it; each receipt names its lists by the same sha256, size and count of lines, and gives each its source key and m id. Relay v188.1's receipts name the lists by the builders' own file names (made-spaces-v1.jsonl, made-spaces-v2.jsonl) and give the bytes of the files as shipped, so a list is matched to its receipt by its bytes, never by its name. Relay v178's receipt says of the Wikisource Strong's that none of its served texts holds a made space, and relay v188.1's says so again, so it has no list
